cleanIntro: This guide comes from Laugo's own book for the Alien pistol. The Alien does not strip like most pistols, so read this first. The barrel is fixed to the frame and never comes out. The top of the gun is in two pieces. The upper rail carries the sights and stays still when you fire. The slide under it runs on a gas piston. So the field strip is the rail off, then the slide, piston and recoil spring together. Laugo's warning about the sear is the one thing here that can hurt you.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber empty — look and feel
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and push the magazine release. The release can be fitted on either side, so it may not be where you expect. Pull the magazine free. Then pull the slide fully to the rear and look into the chamber. Put a finger in the chamber too, because a cartridge can hide in a dark port. Laugo puts this check in capitals at the head of the stripping section. Nothing after this step is safe with a round in the gun.
steps.quote: MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO CARTRIDGES IN THE CHAMBER!
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Dry fire, then cock it again
steps.action: With the gun empty, dry fire it once. Then pull the slide back and let it go, so the trigger mechanism is cocked again. It feels backwards, but it is on purpose. Laugo wants the hammer cocked while the gun is apart and while you put it back together. Skip the re-cock and you will be tempted to lower the hammer by hand later, which the book forbids.
steps.quote: Pull and release the slide so that the trigger mechanism is in the loaded position (fig. 4, 5)
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6
steps.warn: Keep the hammer cocked while the pistol is apart and while you reassemble it.

steps.title: Front locking pin out to its stop
steps.action: Find the front locking pin near the front of the gun. Push it in from one side, then pull it out from the other side as far as it goes. It does not come out of the gun. It stops at its outer position, and that stop is how you know it is free. If it will not move, check that the slide is fully forward. Do not use a tool on it.
steps.quote: Push the front locking pin (fig. 6) and pull it to its outermost position (fig. 7)
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Thumb hard on the back of the upper rail
steps.action: Hold the pistol in your shooting hand. Put your thumb on the back end of the upper rail, the part with the rear sight. Push it forward, hard, until it lets go. It takes real force and it lets go all at once. Keep your other hand around the rail so it does not jump off the gun.
steps.quote: With the thumb of your shooting hand, push hard on the rear of the upper rail (fig. 8) until it has been released (fig. 9).
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Upper rail off, forward and up
steps.action: Lift the upper rail away forward and upward, in one motion. It comes off whole, sights and all. Put it down with the sights facing up so you do not knock the sight adjustment. Nothing is under spring load here, so if it binds, stop and push it straight back rather than pulling at an angle.
steps.quote: Remove the upper rail in a forward upward movement (fig. 10).
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Slide back a little, then up
steps.action: Now the slide is on top. Pull it back only a little, then lift it up off the frame. Only a short pull is needed. The slide is free once it clears its catch, and pulling it all the way back works against you. Hold it gently, because the recoil spring and piston are still hooked to it.
steps.quote: Slightly pull the slide backwards (fig. 11) and up (fig. 12).
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Piston and recoil spring come out with the slide
steps.action: Take the piston and recoil spring assembly out together with the slide. Do not pull the spring off on its own. They leave as one piece, and they go back as one piece too. The piston is the part that needs the most cleaning on this gun, so keep it together and set it aside.
steps.quote: Remove the piston and recoil spring assembly together with the slide (fig. 13).
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You now have the frame with its fixed barrel, the upper rail, the slide, the piston and recoil spring assembly, and the magazine. Laugo says this is far enough for regular maintenance. Stop here. The hammer is exposed now. Laugo's warning on this page is to never release the hammer by pushing on the sear. Leave the trigger parts alone and clean around them.
steps.quote: Stripping the pistol up to this point (fig. 14) is sufficient for regular maintenance.
steps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.8
steps.warn: Never release the hammer by pushing on the sear (fig. 16).

deepSteps.title: The piston chamber — the part this gun is built around
deepSteps.action: Laugo says the piston system needs the most regular care on this pistol. Carbon builds up in the piston chamber and on the piston when you shoot a lot. Put Laugo's Carbon Remover on the piston chamber and the piston. Let it work for about ten minutes. Then clean the whole chamber with the L-shaped cleaner from the accessories, using a circular motion. Brush the piston clean. The book allows metal tools only for carbon a brush will not shift.
deepSteps.quote: Use the Carbon Remover supplied by the manufacturer to clean the piston and the piston chamber.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 7, Cleaning and Preservation, p.10

deepSteps.title: Magazine: slide the base pad back
deepSteps.action: Laugo says to strip the magazine after you have fired a lot. The base pad slides at the back. Move it back to its disassembly position, then push the baseplate forward a little. Point the base of the magazine away from your face before you start. The spring is still pushing on the baseplate.
deepSteps.quote: The magazine has a sliding base pad at the back.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.8

deepSteps.title: Thumb over the baseplate, then take it off
deepSteps.action: Keep your thumb over the baseplate to hold the spring in. With your other hand, take the baseplate off. Then let the spring come up slowly under your thumb. The spring is what can hurt you here. If you take your thumb away too early, it shoots out of the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: Then place your thumb above the baseplate to secure the spring and with your other hand, remove the baseplate completely.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.8
deepSteps.warn: Exercise great caution during this disassembly to prevent injury by the ejected spring.

deepSteps.title: No further — Laugo stops here
deepSteps.action: The book ends the stripping here. It does not show any further disassembly of the pistol. If the gun needs adjusting or repairing, Laugo sends you to a specialized workshop. The trigger mechanism, the hammer and the frame parts are not for the owner to take apart.
deepSteps.quote: Do not disassemble any other parts of the pistol.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN Pistol Instruction Manual — 2021-9 — read from the file name the maker publishes it under; no edition code is printed in the text layer — Section 6, Stripping and Assembly Instructions, p.8

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: The barrel is fixed, so clean from the chamber end with the frame stripped
If the gun is new or lightly fired, push a dry cloth on a rod through, or use a bore snake, until it comes out clean
If the bore is heavily fouled, brush cleaning fluid into the bore and chamber, leave it about 10 minutes, then brush
Dry the bore and chamber with a clean cloth and check that all residue is gone. Repeat if needed
Push the brush through the full length of the barrel before you change direction, or it can stick

cleaning.name: PISTON SYSTEM
tasks: Carbon Remover on the piston chamber and the piston, left about 10 minutes
The L-shaped cleaner from the accessories, turned in a circle around the whole piston chamber
Brush the piston clean. Use metal tools only for carbon a brush cannot remove

cleaning.name: SLIDE, RAIL & FRAME
tasks: Dry cloth, toothbrush, brass brush or wooden scraper on the other parts, including the outside of the barrel
Never the bore solution here, because it sits in the gaps and causes corrosion later
Check that no bits of cloth or bristle are left anywhere in the pistol
Leave the hammer cocked, and never press on the sear

cleaning.name: PRESERVATION
tasks: Once everything is clean and dry, wipe it with a cloth damp with preservation oil, or use spray oil
Wipe off the extra oil, and wipe the bore dry before you shoot
In the cold, remove the oil or use a lubricant made for low temperatures
Use preservation grease only for long storage in bad weather, and take it all off before use

reassembly: Check the hammer is still cocked. Laugo says to keep it cocked while you assemble.
Put the piston and recoil spring assembly back in.
Hook the slide onto the recoil spring assembly, then pull it slightly back and down into place.
Set the upper rail with the sights in position, then push it hard to the rear until you feel it click.
Push the front locking pin back in until it is flush.
Magazine: the stripping steps in reverse. Hold the spring down under your thumb and slide the baseplate back on until the base pad locks at the back.
fncheck: First make sure the pistol and the magazine are empty, and point the muzzle somewhere safe. Pull the slide back and let it go a few times. It should run smoothly and return fully forward. Check that the upper rail does not move and the front locking pin is flush. Insert the empty magazine and make sure the release holds it. Then press the release and check the magazine drops free. Finish the way Laugo's own unloading steps finish: press the trigger once with the gun empty.
